notice: Science-reviewed knowledge content for the Crew Vitals prototype. This application supports personal trend awareness and human review. It is not a medical diagnostic system. Dashboard demonstration records are simulated X01 data, not actual astronaut measurements. All observations must retain their original provenance and measurement context.

brain.label: Brain and behavior
brain.function: Sleep, mood, stress and alertness are relevant to well-being and daily task performance.
brain.spaceflight_effects: Isolation, confinement, demanding schedules and circadian disruption can affect sleep and behavioral well-being.

cardiovascular.label: Heart and blood vessels
cardiovascular.function: The cardiovascular system circulates blood and helps regulate blood pressure.
cardiovascular.spaceflight_effects: Microgravity-related fluid shifts and cardiovascular adaptation are important areas of human spaceflight research.

metabolic.label: Metabolism
metabolic.function: Metabolism converts nutrients into energy and supports normal body functions.
metabolic.spaceflight_effects: Nutrition, physical activity, stress and mission conditions are relevant to metabolic health.

musculoskeletal.label: Bones and muscles
musculoskeletal.function: Bones and muscles support movement, posture and physical activity.
musculoskeletal.spaceflight_effects: Reduced mechanical loading in microgravity contributes to bone and muscle changes. Exercise is an important spaceflight countermeasure.

immune.label: General health and temperature
immune.function: Body temperature is one observation used when monitoring general health.
immune.spaceflight_effects: Immune and other physiological changes during spaceflight are subjects of ongoing research.

radiation.label: Radiation exposure
radiation.function: Radiation instruments and personal dosimeters provide different types of exposure information.
radiation.spaceflight_effects: Space radiation is a significant human spaceflight hazard, particularly beyond the protection provided by Earth's atmosphere and magnetic field.

sleep_duration.label: Sleep duration
sleep_duration.how_measured: Can be estimated using wrist actigraphy or a wearable device and recorded alongside a crew member's sleep log. The measurement method should be documented.
sleep_duration.why: Sleep patterns are relevant to circadian health, well-being and daily task performance during spaceflight.
self_care: Use the mission-approved sleep schedule.
Record sleep and wake times consistently.
Report persistent sleep difficulties through appropriate crew support channels.
contact_when: Sleep difficulties persist or interfere with daily activities.
The crew member requests additional support.
limitations: Wearable sleep estimates are not equivalent to laboratory sleep studies.
Movement-based devices can misclassify rest and sleep.
Sleep duration alone does not establish sleep quality or fatigue.
No clinically validated sleep alert threshold is defined by this prototype.
D03 is a ground-based bed-rest analog dataset, not direct astronaut sleep data.

mood.label: Mood (self-rated 1–5)
mood.how_measured: A crew member voluntarily reports mood using a simple rating scale from 1 to 5.
mood.why: Isolation, confinement, workload and separation from family can influence psychological well-being during long-duration missions.
self_care: Use available crew support and communication opportunities.
Maintain appropriate social contact with other crew members.
Share concerns with an appropriate trusted support person when desired.
contact_when: The crew member experiences persistent emotional difficulty.
The crew member requests behavioral health support.
Any immediate safety concern or thoughts of self-harm require prompt human support through mission emergency procedures.
limitations: Mood ratings are subjective and depend on personal interpretation.
A simple 1–5 scale is not a clinical mental-health assessment.
A single rating cannot establish a long-term pattern.
The prototype must not diagnose depression or another mental-health condition.

stress.label: Stress (self-rated 1–5)
stress.how_measured: A crew member voluntarily reports perceived stress using a simple rating scale from 1 to 5.
stress.why: Mission demands, isolation, confinement and operational pressures can influence perceived stress.
self_care: Use available crew communication and support opportunities.
Discuss workload concerns through appropriate mission channels.
Use mission-approved well-being resources when available.
contact_when: Stress remains a concern or interferes with daily activities.
The crew member requests additional support.
Any immediate safety concern requires prompt human support.
limitations: Stress ratings are subjective.
A rating does not identify the cause of stress.
A simple scale is not a clinical assessment.
The prototype does not diagnose stress-related disorders.

resting_heart_rate.label: Resting heart rate
resting_heart_rate.how_measured: Can be recorded using a wearable optical sensor, chest-strap monitor or an approved manual pulse measurement method. Device and measurement context should be documented.
resting_heart_rate.why: Heart rate is one cardiovascular observation relevant to studying physiological adaptation during spaceflight.
self_care: Follow approved mission procedures for taking and recording the measurement.
Record relevant context such as recent activity and measurement time.
Report health concerns through the appropriate crew medical channel.
contact_when: The crew member experiences symptoms or concerns alongside an unusual reading.
Repeated readings differ substantially from the individual's usual pattern and require human review.
limitations: Movement, sensor placement and device quality can affect readings.
Exercise, sleep and other factors influence heart rate.
A heart-rate value alone cannot diagnose a cardiovascular condition.
No medical alert threshold is established by this prototype.

systolic_bp.label: Blood pressure (systolic)
systolic_bp.how_measured: Can be recorded using an approved automated blood-pressure monitor according to the device and mission measurement procedures. Systolic pressure is the arterial pressure during heart contraction.
systolic_bp.why: Blood pressure provides information about cardiovascular function and pressure regulation, which are relevant to adaptation in microgravity.
self_care: Follow approved procedures for using the blood-pressure device.
Record the measurement conditions and device information.
Report concerns through the appropriate crew medical channel.
contact_when: Repeated readings raise concern or differ substantially from the individual's usual pattern.
Symptoms occur alongside a reading that concerns the crew member.
limitations: Blood pressure varies with posture, activity and measurement conditions.
Cuff placement and device accuracy affect results.
A single reading cannot establish a medical condition.
The prototype does not classify readings using clinical thresholds.

diastolic_bp.label: Blood pressure (diastolic)
diastolic_bp.how_measured: Recorded using the same approved blood-pressure measurement procedure as systolic pressure. Diastolic pressure is the arterial pressure while the heart relaxes between contractions.
diastolic_bp.why: Together with systolic pressure, diastolic pressure helps describe cardiovascular function and pressure regulation.
self_care: Follow approved procedures for using the blood-pressure device.
Record measurement conditions consistently.
Report concerns through the appropriate crew medical channel.
contact_when: Repeated readings raise concern or differ substantially from the individual's usual pattern.
The crew member experiences symptoms or requests medical review.
limitations: Readings can vary between measurements.
Measurement conditions and equipment influence accuracy.
Diastolic pressure requires appropriate clinical context.
The prototype does not independently classify a reading as medically normal or abnormal.

blood_glucose.label: Blood glucose
blood_glucose.how_measured: Can be measured using an approved blood-glucose meter and an appropriate blood sample. The record should indicate whether the measurement was fasting or non-fasting.
blood_glucose.why: Glucose is an important energy source. Metabolism, nutrition and physical activity are relevant to human health during spaceflight.
self_care: Follow approved mission procedures for glucose measurement.
Record whether the measurement was fasting or non-fasting.
Discuss concerns with the appropriate crew medical professional.
contact_when: A reading raises concern under the applicable medical protocol.
The crew member experiences symptoms or requests medical review.
limitations: Results depend on sampling conditions and device accuracy.
Fasting and non-fasting measurements are not directly interchangeable.
A single reading cannot diagnose diabetes or another metabolic condition.
No glucose alert threshold or treatment instruction is defined by this prototype.

body_temperature.label: Body temperature
body_temperature.how_measured: Can be recorded using an approved thermometer. The measurement method, such as oral or forehead measurement, should be documented.
body_temperature.why: Body temperature is one observation used when monitoring general health and possible physiological changes during a mission.
self_care: Follow the approved thermometer instructions.
Record the measurement method and time.
Report health concerns through the appropriate crew medical channel.
contact_when: The crew member has persistent symptoms or concerns.
A reading raises concern under the applicable mission medical protocol.
limitations: Different measurement methods can produce different readings.
Environmental conditions and measurement technique can affect results.
Temperature alone cannot identify the cause of an illness.
The prototype does not diagnose infection or establish a fever alert threshold.

radiation_badge_daily_dose.label: Daily radiation badge dose
radiation_badge_daily_dose.how_measured: If a personal dosimeter is provided, its recorded value can be entered with the instrument identity, units and measurement period. A manually entered badge value must retain its own provenance.
radiation_badge_daily_dose.why: Space radiation is a significant human spaceflight hazard. Radiation monitoring supports research and mission safety procedures.
self_care: Follow the mission's authorized radiation monitoring and safety procedures.
Use only verified personal dosimeter information when recording an individual measurement.
Refer radiation concerns to the responsible mission personnel.
contact_when: An instrument reading or radiation event requires review under mission procedures.
The crew member has questions about personal exposure or radiation safety.
limitations: A personal badge reading is not automatically equivalent to effective dose or biological risk.
Instrument type, calibration, location and radiation characteristics matter.
NASA environmental instrument readings are not the same as an individual's personal dosimeter reading.
Raw radiation flux or dose-rate data must not be converted into personal cancer risk without validated methods.
The prototype does not issue radiation shelter instructions or determine individual medical risk.

exercise_minutes.label: Exercise duration
exercise_minutes.how_measured: Exercise duration can be recorded using exercise-equipment logs, wearable activity devices or crew-entered records. Aerobic and resistive activity should be distinguished when available.
exercise_minutes.why: Reduced mechanical loading in microgravity contributes to bone and muscle changes. Exercise is an important countermeasure used in human spaceflight.
self_care: Record exercise activity according to mission procedures.
Distinguish aerobic and resistive exercise when the available record permits.
Report exercise-related concerns through the appropriate mission support channel.
contact_when: The crew member experiences pain or other concerns during exercise.
Exercise records indicate a persistent interruption that requires human review.
limitations: Exercise duration does not establish exercise intensity.
Logged minutes do not directly measure muscle strength or bone density.
Equipment and activity type affect interpretation.
Exercise records alone cannot establish countermeasure effectiveness for an individual.

station.label: ISS / Station
station.one_way_delay: Communication is generally near real time, subject to network coverage and mission communication arrangements.
station.reply_expectation: Availability of medical support depends on mission operations and communication links.
station.guidance: Use established mission communication channels and follow authorized crew medical procedures.

spacecraft.label: Spacecraft
spacecraft.one_way_delay: Communication delay depends on spacecraft location, relay availability and communication configuration.
spacecraft.reply_expectation: Communication availability and response time depend on mission operations.
spacecraft.guidance: Follow the mission communication plan and authorized onboard procedures.

lunar.label: Lunar surface
lunar.one_way_delay: Communication delay depends on the spacecraft or surface location and relay configuration.
lunar.reply_expectation: Communication availability depends on line of sight and mission relay infrastructure.
lunar.guidance: Use approved mission communication and medical support procedures.

mars.label: Mars mission
mars.one_way_delay: Communication delay varies with Earth–Mars distance and mission configuration and can be substantial.
mars.reply_expectation: Immediate two-way communication with Earth cannot be assumed.
mars.guidance: Follow authorized onboard medical and emergency procedures. Preserve observations and communicate through the mission-approved process.

environment_note: Communication descriptions are qualitative context, not operational communication guarantees. Exact delay values and response expectations require mission-specific NASA or agency documentation. Do not use these descriptions to replace a mission communication plan.
